A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Attribution-Guided Decoding by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original instruction-following and question-answering experiments in Tables 1, 3, and 7, alongside attribution analyses and decoding ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds head-count, computational-efficiency, and prompt-sensitivity results in Tables 7, 8, and 10.

M1.justification: Candidate selection, attribution scoring, ROI definitions, entropy gating, and attention-head selection remain unchanged. The new experiments test existing components without introducing a new decoding procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain IHEval, SysBench, TriviaQA, Natural Questions, HotPotQA, and NQ-Swap. V2 explicitly describes HotPotQA contexts containing two gold and eight shuffled distractor paragraphs. V1 leaves context construction unspecified, so the PDFs do not establish whether this introduces a different input environment or documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain greedy decoding, nucleus sampling, CAD for instruction following and open-book QA, and DoLA for closed-book QA. The I×G and LRP variant rows are also retained; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix A revises the open-book HotPotQA sample count from 5,913 to 5,918. Added analyses introduce four head-count settings, two prompt formulations, and efficiency measurements over 100 samples with a maximum sequence length of 256 tokens. The existing model sizes, decoding hyperparameters, and benchmark accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands supplementary validation: Table 7 tests sensitivity to selecting 10, 50, 100, or 200 heads; Table 8 measures runtime, memory, and execution passes across three models; and Table 10 tests prompt-ordering and phrasing sensitivity. These address questions beyond v1's retained entropy/probability ablations and attribution case studies.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies five nucleus-sampling runs. This is a disclosed run count, not an established increase over v1. Existing nucleus-sampling uncertainty entries and the fixed-seed statement remain; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Open-book HotPotQA results are replaced across all three models. For example, Table 3 changes Llama greedy recall from 52.4 to 81.3, AGD_LRPh from 57.4 to 87.9, and AGD_LRPc from 59.8 to 87.9; identical evaluation conditions are not established. New tables add head-count, efficiency, and prompt-sensitivity outcomes. V2 also contains a discrepancy: Llama HotPotQA CAD recall is 83.7 in Tables 3 and 10 but 83.4 in Table 9.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same attribution definitions, selection and gating rules, CAD formula, and attention-head extraction mathematics. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about attribution-guided selection, instruction adherence, factuality, interpretability, and entropy gating. The additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix G newly interpret results as evidence of grounding despite distractors and robustness beyond a particular prompt formulation. Appendix D discusses information coverage versus head count, while Appendix E qualifies computational practicality with increased memory use. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies retrieval-context construction details, the alternative prompt template, and efficiency-test hardware and software information: NVIDIA A100 80GB, PyTorch 2.6.0, and bf16. The code pointer changes from the attribution-guided-decoding repository in the conclusion to AGD in the abstract; actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Sclar et al. (2024) to motivate testing sensitivity to prompt formatting. The remaining bibliography and the positioning of AGD relative to activation steering, contrastive decoding, and attribution methods are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized expansions to Section 5 and the appendices, inserts efficiency and prompt-sensitivity sections, reorders acknowledgments and the reproducibility statement, adds funding acknowledgments and conference headers, and corrects small textual errors. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables for head counts, efficiency, and prompt sensitivity. V1 Table 7 becomes v2 Table 9, and existing appendix figures are relocated without changed visual content. Figure 2 corrects 'Inclustion' to 'Inclusion'; other changes are limited caption and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new head-count and prompt-sensitivity tests, measured runtime and memory costs, and implementation details make robustness and practical tradeoffs better supported than in v1. These benefits provide a limited net improvement, tempered by unclear comparability of the replaced HotPotQA results and the inconsistent CAD value across v2 Tables 3, 9, and 10.
